newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan smelter Onahama warily eyes water shortage.
newsitem.headline: Japan smelter Onahama warily eyes water shortage.

text.p: Onahama Smelting and Refining Co said on Friday it was warily eyeing one of the worst water shortages this century in its prefecture of Fukushima, although a recent 30 percent cut in water supplies to industrial users would not affect its copper output.

He added, however, that while rains late this week helped ensure that the cutback would be limited to 30 percent through the first 10 days of September, further cuts may be needed if there is no additional rainfall during that time.
Water cutbacks significantly beyond the 30 percent mark could affect operations, he said, although it was too early to determine how much production might be lost.

The Onahama copper refinery, owned by six Japanese copper companies including Mitsubishi Materials Corp and Dowa Mining Co, is Japan's largest with a refining capacity of about 250,000 tonnes of cathodes annually.
